TITLE: Low-Computational-Budget Low-Shot Evaluation of Efficient Forecasting Baselines
PROPOSAL: Compare the forecasting performance of state-of-the-art artificial neural network (ANN) architectures (LSTM and GRU) and a lightweight transformer model (MiniLM) on four benchmark datasets (M5, M4, Electricity, and Train station arrivals) with various training data sizes, from few-shot (<10 examples) to regular (full) training, to gauge their relative sensitivity to data availability.
CONTROLS: Regular-followed-by-truncated versus truncated-only training for each model.
COST: 30 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: Small ANN models will perform best under low-shot conditions, while the MiniLM model's pre-trained weights will allow it to outperform all other models with full training, indicating limited robustness regarding in-distribution overfitting and sensitivity to low data quantities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mitigating Energy Bias in Sparse Transformers for Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of novel modifications to sparse mixture-of-experts Transformers that directly address energy bias: (1) bypassing self-attention via frequency-aware feedforward paths; (2) incorporating low-energy attention weights via penalty terms; and (3) utilizing attention residual learned construction to capture informative low-energy patterns.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline model with standard sparse attention weights and self-attention-only architecture.
COST: 60 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: Modifications will mitigate energy bias and allow the model to capture persistent, informative patterns at various frequencies, producing better generalization to unseen domains and improving model robustness, particularly for low-amplitude informative patterns. However, the performance may degrade for tasks dominated by high-energy frequency components.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Mitigating Energy Bias in Sparse Transformers for Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 2 to incorporate a separate energy-aware loss term that penalizes the model for its energy bias during pre-training, preserving the original architecture structure and not bypassing self-attention via feedforward paths or incorporating low-energy attention weights via penalties. The energy-aware loss will be added to the standard MSELoss during pre-training to learn the importance of all frequency components.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline model with standard MSELoss and against proposal 2 without the energy-aware loss term.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (estimated reduction due to simpler architecture modifications).
PREDICTION: This modification will enable more efficient learning of low-energy frequency patterns, but unlike the previous suggestion, might not benefit quickly from low-amplitude features in rich signal scenarios.

ACTION: REVISE 2

PROPOSAL: As previously proposed, modify the sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer to include an energy-aware loss term during pre-training, penalizing the model for its energy bias. CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline model with standard MSELoss and regular pre-training scheme.
COST: 40 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: Training with early-stopping or a learning rate decay will have a positive effect by reducing the energy bias and allowing the model to generalize better across various distributions. Dropout during pre-training should also contribute to more effective learning and allow the model to handle complexities related to energy patterns.

TITLE: Mini-Transformer in Mini-Dataset

The goal is to analyze if a significantly reduced model size can still capture domain-agnostic patterns, indicating potential for more efficient time series forecasting. 
CONTROLS: Perform evaluation at 10%, 20%, and 50% of the full model size, validating that the decreased size affects performance and against a baseline that is the same architecture and training data, but before compression.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Revised Lightweight CNN-Based Architecture
PROPOSAL: We propose a revised CNN architecture, instead of using 1D convolutional layers, utilizing a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) structure for time series forecasting with reduced complexity. TCNs have been shown to effectively capture temporal relationships in time series data. In this experiment, we'll pre-train the revised TCN model using the 80% Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) dataset and evaluate its zero-shot generalization to new datasets, such as traffic forecasting, solar power forecasting, and cloud operations monitoring, using their respective benchmarks. The goal is to assess the adaptability of this design across diverse domains.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised TCN model against the mini-Transformer in mini-dataset (proposal 1), the sparse temporal attention mechanism (proposal 2), and a baseline that is the same architecture and training data, but before parameter reduction.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (evaluating across multiple benchmarks).
PREDICTION: The revised TCN model should show promising adaptability across different domains due to its ability to capture temporal relationships, and it might even outperform the mini-Transformer and sparse attention mechanism in certain cases.

Note: To ensure efficiency and highlight the strengths of the revised TCN model, this experiment focuses on adaptability across different domains rather than in-depth analysis within a single domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utility-Based Pruning for Model Size Reduction
PROPOSAL: We aim to further reduce the model size of the existing proposals by utilizing a utility-based pruning method, which selectively removes the least important parameters based on their contribution to the model's performance. This pruning method will be applied to the top-performing previous proposals (e.g., the revised TCN architecture) and evaluated on the Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) dataset. By applying this pruning technique, we expect to retain the essential parameters while reducing the model size and computational requirements.
CONTROLS: Compare the pruned models against their original counterparts and a baseline that is the same architecture but without pruning.
COST: 15 GPU-hours (pruning and re-training).
PREDICTION: The pruned models are expected to retain a majority of their original performance while significantly reducing the model size, making them more suitable for resource-constrained environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Few-Shot Learning for Transferability Enhancement
PROPOSAL: We explore the use of few-shot learning techniques to enhance the transferability of the existing proposals across different domains. Specifically, we will use the replay buffer from meta-learning to adapt the learned knowledge from one domain to another. This approach will be evaluated on the Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) dataset, traffic forecasting, solar power forecasting, and cloud operations monitoring benchmarks. By leveraging few-shot learning, we aim to improve the model's ability to generalize to unseen domains and datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the few-shot learning approach against the existing proposals (e.g., revised TCN architecture) and a baseline that is the same architecture but without few-shot learning.
COST: 60 GPU-hours (few-shot learning and adaptation).
PREDICTION: Few-shot learning is expected to enhance the transferability of the existing proposals, allowing them to generalize better to unseen domains and datasets, particularly when pre-trained on a smaller dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subvector Attention Mechanism
PROPOSAL: We propose an alternative attention mechanism, referred to as subvector attention, to specifically address the challenge of capturing low-energy frequency components in time series data. This mechanism involves learning to selectively attend to specific subvectors of the input sequence, rather than computing attention weights over the entire sequence. We will evaluate this subvector attention mechanism on the Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) dataset and compare its performance against the state-of-the-art sparse temporal attention mechanism (proposal 2). Additionally, we will investigate the effectiveness of combining subvector attention with few-shot learning (proposal 5) for transferability enhancement.
CONTROLS: Compare the subvector attention mechanism against the sparse temporal attention mechanism, the existing proposals (e.g., revised TCN architecture), and a baseline that is the same architecture but without subvector attention.
COST: 45 GPU-hours (training and evaluation).
PREDICTION: The subvector attention mechanism is expected to provide comparable or improved performance to the sparse temporal attention mechanism, particularly for time series data with prominent low-energy frequency components. When combined with few-shot learning, the subvector attention mechanism may exhibit enhanced transferability across domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distillation-Based Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: We aim to transfer the knowledge learned from the best-performing proposals to a smaller, pre-trained model, leveraging knowledge distillation techniques. Specifically, we will use the pre-trained lightweight CNN-based architecture (proposal 3) as the teacher network and fine-tune its knowledge to match the performance of the top-performing proposals (e.g., revised TCN architecture) on the Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) dataset. This approach enables us to leverage the strengths of both the teacher network and the top-performing proposals while reducing the computational requirements.
CONTROLS: Compare the knowledge distillation approach against the top-performing proposals, the existing proposals (e.g., subvector attention mechanism), and a baseline that is the same pre-trained CNN-based architecture without fine-tuning.
COST: 30 GPU-hours (knowledge distillation and fine-tuning).
PREDICTION: The knowledge distillation approach is expected to enable the pre-trained CNN-based architecture to match the performance of the top-performing proposals, while reducing the computational requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Comparison and Evaluation
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive comparison of the performance and efficiency of the top-performing proposals across various metrics, including zero-shot transferability, few-shot learning, and competitive benchmarking on the Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) dataset, traffic forecasting, solar power forecasting, and cloud operations monitoring benchmarks. This comparison will help identify the most effective combinations of techniques for achieving strong zero- and few-shot generalization in time series forecasting, while highlighting areas where further research is needed.
CONTROLS: Include all top-performing proposals, knowledge distillation approach, and competitive baselines in the comprehensive comparison and evaluation.
COST: 80 GPU-hours (comprehensive evaluation and comparison).
PREDICTION: This comprehensive comparison will provide a thorough understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each proposal, enabling us to identify the most effective approaches for achieving zero- and few-shot generalization in time series forecasting and to establish a foundation for future research in this area.
